#### 1. autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2C  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.509)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-917977, Reactome:R-HSA-983712, Reactome:R-HSA-1222556, Reactome:R-HSA-77387)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6V1E1 (HGNC:14252) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0016068); ATP6V0A4 (HGNC:14247) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0016068); V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0016068) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue (HP:0003549); V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0016068) —LEADS_TO→ Generalized arterial calcification of infancy (HP:0030184); V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0016068) —LEADS_TO→ Cutis laxa (HP:0000970). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP6V1E1 (causing autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2C) and ATP6V0A4 (causing generalized arterial calcification of infancy 1) disrupt the assembly and function of the V-ATPase complex. This shared disruption leads to downstream cellular defects that manifest as abnormal connective tissue, cutis laxa, and arterial calcification.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ATP6V1E1 or ATP6V0A4 that do not lead to a detectable disruption in V-ATPase complex assembly or function, or the absence of any shared connective tissue phenotypes between affected individuals. _(variant: rs750653734 (gnomAD allele frequency > 1%))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of V-ATPase complex dysfunction in these distinct but mechanistically linked diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for improving connective tissue integrity and vascular health.
